    {
      "startEvent": 785,
      "endEvent": 794,
      "contextStartEvent": 727,
      "contextEndEvent": 819,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "just because we can't comprehend any possible reason doesn't mean there aren't any",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The initial possibility claim is legitimate, but E792-E794 turn an inability to find reasons into assurance that reasons exceed our capacity. This supplies no connection between permitted atrocities and divine goodness while sheltering that connection from the objection. A fairly rejects compulsory greater-good stories and acknowledges limited understanding at E760-E784."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1116,
      "endEvent": 1125,
      "contextStartEvent": 1066,
      "contextEndEvent": 1133,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "he knows our motives he knows our past he knows our heart",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Asked whether punishing sincere nonbelief is consistent with love, A invokes inaccessible personal knowledge and perfect judgment instead of resolving the stipulated case. That protects the justice of the verdict through unseen considerations. This is an explanatory theological argument, not a slogan; fairly, A also refuses to pronounce any individual's destination at E1110."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1126,
      "endEvent": 1133,
      "contextStartEvent": 1105,
      "contextEndEvent": 1133,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "because you know in your heart of hearts that it is just grossly wrong",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B interprets A's appeal to limited knowledge as concealed agreement with his objection, without evidence of her internal belief. This could neutralize her qualification by assigning an ulterior explanation. However, E1132-E1133 explicitly mark it as his interpretation, and the exchange does not establish a general rule dismissing contrary arguments."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1196,
      "endEvent": 1208,
      "contextStartEvent": 1134,
      "contextEndEvent": 1216,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "everyone that asks for healing will be healed",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Healing confirms heaven's arrival at E1180-E1184; nonhealing means continuing brokenness, with eventual healing guaranteed at E1196-E1208. The account supplies no reason for selective intervention and makes either outcome compatible with the promise. A acknowledges mystery and pain and explicitly rejects blaming patients' faith, prayer, or wrongdoing at E1190-E1195."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1351,
      "endEvent": 1370,
      "contextStartEvent": 1305,
      "contextEndEvent": 1370,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "God is not not that binary",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After B contrasts fatal nonhealing with allegedly unnecessary limb restoration, A invokes complexity, unconditional love, and the slot-machine analogy. These replace an explanation of selective help and insulate divine care from either outcome. Fairly, A previously offers a contact for the limb claim and accepts spontaneous remission at E1305-E1316."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1652,
      "endEvent": 1661,
      "contextStartEvent": 1572,
      "contextEndEvent": 1661,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "God is good he doesn't carry out miscarriages of Justice",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The assurance leaves the moral atheist's fate unresolved and may function as a guarantee that any eventual disposition is just. However, E1579-E1650 offer actual reasons involving earthly accountability, costly forgiveness, repentance, and transformation. Those reasons make it uncertain whether this conclusion substitutes for argument or expressly overrides every contrary case."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1677,
      "endEvent": 1682,
      "contextStartEvent": 1572,
      "contextEndEvent": 1694,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "they can't answer them and they have to talk about Jesus and love",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "ridicule"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B generalizes from this response to an inability to answer difficult questions and treats its length and theological content as evidence of evasion. That generalization is unsupported, but his specific objection concerning unequal salvation conditions is stated at E1666-E1676. It remains unclear whether the refrain replaces that argument or forecloses substantive replies."
    }

  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 708,
      "endEvent": 710,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "sometimes good things can come out of suffering but the good that can come out of it isn't the reason that it happened",
      "explanation": "Explicitly distinguishes beneficial consequences from reasons for an event. E674-E707 reject insensitive attempts to assign personal purposes to suffering, and E760-E777 renew the qualification that good need not follow every atrocity."
